Within each race, there stirs a longing.

It is not oppressive. Many would call it harmless. A minor wave of wanderlust, inspiring a wistful poem here or there, or the occasional picture of lands never seen, seldom imagined. A few take walks longer than they normally would take, call it an adventure, and sleep smiling. There is an odd surge in the popularity of extra-heavy blankets.

All in all, nothing to worry about.

But a few... Oh, a few. They toss and turn and cannot rest easy. They cannot hide from their own feet, and their feet point due 'away,' ache restlessly. They gather around the wells and water-places. Expecting to be alone with their new, unfamiliar thoughts, they instead find companions, besotted by much the same thing. Excitedly, they talk, excitedly, as apprehensive and shy as first-time lovers. But they grow bolder. Tearfully, they confess to their parents that they will not take over the family shop, or that it will fall to someone else to raise the next Honeycattle brood. The packs are packed. The saddles saddled. The farewells spoken.

There are not many of them. A dozen here, a dozen there. But they hail from every corner.
